item.name: Purchase Requests
item.description: Task 08B-1/08B-2: company-scoped Purchase Request draft/submit/cancel/approve/reject/revise APIs. Every request here requires {{access_token}} to belong to a user with an ACTIVE CompanyMembership in {{company_id}} AND the specific purchase_requests.* permission each action needs - a superuser login alone is NOT enough (no administrative-read bypass exists for this resource, unlike the Task 07B catalog folders above). An administrator must first: create/assign a company role holding purchase_requests.view/create/edit/submit/cancel (see folder 9, 'Company Role Management' - 'Replace role permissions' with these codes), then assign that role to the member who will run requests 1-6. Requests 7-9 (approve/reject/revise) need a SECOND ordinary member holding purchase_requests.view/approve, logged in separately (see the note before request 7) - the requester can never decide their own request, with no exception. Run folder 15's 'Create material' first so {{material_id}} refers to a real, active material. SUBMITTED never means approved on its own - it starts a three-step approval round. Running this folder creates and mutates real development-database records - see README.md. Manual Postman execution is deferred.

item.name: Incoming QC Inspections
item.description: Task 09B-1: manually-entered QC inspection DRAFTS against an already-POSTED goods-receipt line, at a shared store. This records that observations were taken only - it never decides acceptance/rejection, never releases material, never creates stock, and never changes the source receipt's quantities. Every request needs {{access_token}} to belong to a user holding BOTH an active StoreMembership in {{store_id}} with the specific incoming_qc.* permission each action needs, AND active CompanyMembership (bare membership only - no purchase_orders.view required, unlike Goods Receipts) in the receipt line's own purchasing company - see docs/incoming-qc-proposal.md. Run folder 20 (Goods Receipts) through 'Post goods receipt' first, so {{goods_receipt_id}} refers to a real POSTED receipt with at least one line. Running this folder creates and mutates real development-database records - see README.md. Manual Postman execution is deferred. Task 09B-3A adds real submission: requests 7-12 demonstrate creating a second draft against the same (now-freed, since request 6 cancelled the first) receipt line, the required-observation validation at submit time, a successful submit recording submitted_by/submitted_at, and that a SUBMITTED inspection can no longer be edited or cancelled through any endpoint.

item.name: Customer Management
item.description: Task 10A: company-scoped customer identity/contact directory - the foundation for a future quotations/sales-order chain that does not exist yet anywhere in this project. COMPANY-SCOPING HERE IS THE WORKING IMPLEMENTATION CHOICE FOR THIS TASK, NOT A CLAIM OF CLIENT-CONFIRMED CUSTOMER-OWNERSHIP POLICY (see docs/erp-handoff-open-decisions.md §A13) - unlike Supplier Management (folder 17), which is one directory shared across both companies, each Customer row belongs to exactly one company, and its code is unique per company only (the same code may exist under a different company). Five new COMPANY-scope permissions gate this folder: customers.view, customers.create, customers.edit, customers.activate, customers.deactivate - seeded but assigned to nobody automatically, so {{access_token}} must belong to a user with an active membership and the relevant role in {{company_id}} (see folder 9's "Company Role Management" to grant these). No DELETE exists anywhere in this module - deactivating never deletes the record, and a deactivated customer's code is never freed for reuse within the same company. This is an identity/contact record only - no quotation, sales order, invoice, GST/PAN, credit limit, payment terms, or customer-qualification concept exists anywhere here. Running this folder creates and mutates real development-database records - see README.md. Manual Postman execution is deferred.

request.description: material_requisitions.view + .submit (store) + batch_plans.view + formulas.view (company). Freezes the request as SUBMITTED - does NOT approve quantities, reserve stock, issue materials, authorize production or release anything from QC. A repeat call at the current version is an idempotent no-op; every header/line edit is rejected (400) once SUBMITTED.

material_requisitions.view + .approve (store) + batch_plans.view + formulas.view (company). Only a SUBMITTED requisition can be approved. Blocked (400) if the actor is the requisition's own creator, the current round's submitter, or made a substantive requested_quantity change currently reflected on any line - no exception. A repeat call at the current (already-APPROVED) version is an idempotent no-op, preserving the original decided_by/decided_at.

Same permission (material_requisitions.view + .approve) and self-decision ban as approve - there is no separate .reject permission. rejection_reason is required (non-blank). Unlike approve, rejection never re-checks source drift - a drift that blocks approval never blocks rejection, since rejection's purpose is to send the request back for correction. A repeat call at the current version with the SAME reason is an idempotent no-op; the same call with a DIFFERENT reason is 409, never silently applied.

material_requisitions.view + .edit + .revise (store) + batch_plans.view + formulas.view (company) - revising reopens editable data, so .edit is additionally required here, unlike approve/reject/submit. Only a REJECTED requisition can be revised, back to DRAFT. Plain reopen (no quantity-affecting source drift): lines carry forward completely unchanged. If the source HAS drifted, this same call is rejected (400) unless the body also includes refresh_from_source:true and the CURRENT expected_batch_plan_version (a stale plan version is 409) - see docs/frontend-api-handoff.md §18.10 for the full refresh contract. Every prior round's own submission and decision is permanently preserved, never touched by this action.
